key_insight: Thermal tensile strain on silicon stabilizes ideal antiferroelectric domain behavior in epitaxial PbZrO3, enabling direct one-step switching with large, reversible electromechanical response.
engineering_relevance: This work shows a silicon-compatible path to fast, low-remanence antiferroelectric devices with strong electrostrain for nanoelectronic and actuator applications.
method: Grow epitaxial PbZrO3 thin films on silicon to exploit thermal mismatch as tensile strain
Use combined theory and experiments to link strain state with domain type and switching pathway
Compare tensile-strain (004)o domains against compressive-strain (240)o domains to identify ideal antiferroelectric behavior
evidence_signal: The films show near-zero remanent polarization, square double hysteresis, ~75 ns switching, and reversible electrostrain of about 0.6% under the engineered strain state.
watch_item: Device performance may depend strongly on strain-controlled domain stability and film integration quality, so scaling and long-term reliability on silicon need further validation.
paper_title: Silicon-compatible ideal antiferroelectricity with large digital electromechanical responses enabled by thermal-strain domain engineering
